messages:
maria: Kicking off the Ambrosia region account priming. Need VPC scaffold, GPU quota request, NAT topology, and a short smoke validation plan so we can hand off to delivery by EOD tomorrow. TL;DR: gcp project, shared VPC, two private subnets for GPU nodes, public bastion, egress NAT+cost estimate.

own: +1. What CIDR range are we carving for the cluster subnets? We should avoid overlapping with EU networks (10.40.0.0/16 used there). Propose 10.80.0.0/16 for cluster, split into /19 for gpu-pools and /20 for infra.

sasha: We also need a list of required firewall rules for peerings and control plane traffic (health checks from LB, GKE control plane IP ranges) and whether we expect Cloud NAT or NAT gateways per subnet. Cloud NAT is cheaper but has ephemeral port limits.

maria: Plan: project: redwood-ambrosia-core, shared-vpc host: redwood-global-vpc. Cluster CIDR: 10.80.0.0/16. Subnets: 10.80.0.0/19 (gpu-pool-1), 10.80.32.0/20 (gpu-pool-2), 10.80.48.0/22 (infra), bastion public /27. Use Cloud NAT with 2 NAT gateways to spread ephemeral ports; fallback to dedicated NAT gateway if we hit port saturation.

kim: For GPU quota, open a ticket to cloud-provider with the model: "accelerator quota increase: nvidia-t4: 40, a100-80gb: 8". I can submit but need the justification text. Use: "production inference farm for Ambrosia region, expected sustained throughput 20K tokens/sec, will be on Redwood Dedicated."

maria: Thanks. Kim, can you submit and cc @owen for networking details? Add tag: priority=high.

kim: Submitted: ticket #CP-82411, ETA 48-72h. I pasted the justification. deploy-bot: quota_request_created CP-82411 by kim.

deploy-bot: Quota ticket CP-82411 updated: status=OPEN, requested_resources=[t4:40,a100-80:8], submitted_by=kim. ETA=48-72h.

own: On peering: we need VPC peering to prod-logging and to platform-services (metrics, image registry). Recommend using a TGW (hub-and-spoke) pattern so we don't create n^2 peering. If provider supports it, create a shared-router in the host project and attach spokes.

sasha: Validation checklist draft: 
- Verify project IAM: infra-group has Editor on host VPC, cluster-sa has compute.networkAdmin minimal perms
- Subnet creation and route table validation (no default internet route from private subnets)
- Cloud NAT config and ephemeral port test (run 500 concurrent TCP flows from 1k pods simulated)
- GPU node startup: a100 node boots, attaches to subnet, kubelet registers within 3 minutes
- KV cache egress test: ping platform-registry and metrics endoints; ensure MTU negotiation ok
- Cost smoke: run bench run for 1 hour to estimate egress and NAT SNAT consumption

maria: Add: security controls: ensure no external SSH open on gpu subnets; bastion in infra subnet with restricted source ranges only. Also set VPC firewall to allow health-checks from cloud-lb ranges only.

kim: Small config snippet for gcloud infra that I used for bootstrap: 
```
gcloud compute networks create redwood-ambrosia-vpc --subnet-mode=custom
gcloud compute networks subnets create gpu-pool-1 --network=redwood-ambrosia-vpc --region=ambrosia-region --range=10.80.0.0/19
gcloud compute networks subnets create gpu-pool-2 --network=redwood-ambrosia-vpc --region=ambrosia-region --range=10.80.32.0/20
gcloud compute routers create nat-router-1 --network=redwood-ambrosia-vpc --region=ambrosia-region
gcloud compute routers nats create nat-1 --router=nat-router-1 --auto-allocate-nat-external-ips --nat-custom-subnet-ip-ranges=gpu-pool-1,gpu-pool-2,infra-subnet
```

maria: I'll run through a dry-run tomorrow morning and post the smoke command. Owen, can you validate the TGW design with netops? Also we'll need to provision a private DNS zone for service discovery (registry.redwood.internal).

own: Will validate with netops. Two notes: 1) check NAT egress billing for cross-region egress to metrics (we may be charged), 2) check if cloud provider has preemptible quotas for T4s — we prefer preemptible for batch but reserved for Dedicated inference.

sasha: For smoke validation, my quick run command (k8s job) to spawn ephemeral clients: 
```
kubectl run sockbench --image=ghcr.io/redwood/sockbench:latest --replicas=200 --command -- /bin/sh -c "for i in 1..100; do curl -sS https://metrics.redwood.internal/health; done"
```

maria: Nice. I'll collect results and attach to the handoff doc. Who's owning the final delivery ticket? I nominate Owen for networking handoff, Sasha for validation, Kim for quota and bootstrap scripts. I'll be overall PM.

owen: ack. I'll create the delivery ticket and add acceptance criteria (routes, peering, NAT perf, firewall, DNS).

kim: I'll share bootstrap GCP IAM bindings and the terraform module draft in 
`/infra/terraform/modules/ambrosia-vpc` in the repo. Expect PR by EOD.

maria: Great. Final ask: can everyone drop one-liners when their item is done in this thread so we have a concise handoff history? :thumbsup:

sasha: Will post validation summary here once tests complete.

deploy-bot: ticket CP-82411 status=OPEN -> UPDATED by kim.

maria: Thanks all — let's aim for handoff by 16:00 UTC tomorrow.
